features.text: The patient is a 74-year-old male.
The patient has had a cough for about a week, which has been worsening over the last two days.
The patient is bringing up yellow sputum.
The patient is not experiencing chest pain or shortness of breath.
The patient feels a little achy sometimes.
The patient does not have a history of previous respiratory illnesses or surgeries.
The patient does not have allergies.
The patient does not have a family history of respiratory conditions.
The patient twisted his right knee and fell down the stairs this morning.
The patient has pain on the right knee, mostly on the inside.
The patient has some bruising on the right knee.
The patient can still walk on the right knee but experiences pain when putting weight on it and has a slight limp.
The patient does not have a history of previous knee injuries or surgeries.
The patient's temperature is 98.4°F.
The patient's blood pressure is 125/62 mmHg.
The patient's oxygen level is 97% on room air.
The doctor heard coarse rhonchi in the lungs that cleared with coughing.
The patient experiences pain when the doctor presses on the right knee.
The patient has not had any recent chest X-rays or sputum cultures.
The patient has not had any imaging or lab tests for the knee injury yet.
The patient has not experienced weight loss, night sweats, or hemoptysis.
The patient has not been exposed to environmental irritants such as smoke, dust, or chemicals in the past week.
The patient has not had any prior orthopedic evaluations or imaging for knee injuries.
The patient slipped and fell down about four or five stairs while coughing, without hearing a popping sound or feeling instability in the knee.
The patient has not had any prior imaging or evaluation of the right knee following this injury.
The patient has not had any recent chest imaging or sputum culture to evaluate the productive cough and yellow sputum.
